canonical_question: What should I understand about I/O buffer size, and why does it matter in Logic Pro?
clarification_questions: Is the delayed thing a microphone/instrument monitor, a software instrument, or the placement of the recorded region?
Does the delay exist in an empty project, only through Logic, only through direct monitoring, or only after specific plug-ins are active?
What interface, sample rate, I/O buffer, monitoring path, Low Latency Mode state, and high-latency plug-ins are involved?

competing_hypotheses.description: I/O buffer size or another audio/MIDI stage is adding real monitoring or placement latency.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 1

competing_hypotheses.description: Duplicate monitoring, high-latency routing, driver/device state, or project complexity is being mistaken for one buffer problem.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 2

competing_hypotheses.description: direct monitoring or freezing/bypassing heavy processing would provide a cleaner diagnostic or lower-latency recording path.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 3

direct_answer: Buffer size trades monitoring latency against processing stability; choose the smallest stable setting for the current recording task. In Logic, first prove which stage or container owns the problem, then change only that stage and compare against the preserved baseline.
evidence_needed: The exact Logic version, device/interface, input/output routing, record and monitor state, relevant preferences, and current project/track/container state.
A preserved baseline plus one controlled test using the same performer, phrase, cue, and playback conditions.
Meters or recorded regions at each relevant signal-flow checkpoint, along with any audible delay, duplication, click, dropout, changed take, or placement error.
The user’s report of what improved, worsened, stayed unchanged, or became harder to perform after the test.
key_distinction: Buffer size trades monitoring latency against processing stability; choose the smallest stable setting for the current recording task.
limitations: A meter, waveform, region position, or setting does not by itself prove the performer heard or recorded the intended result.
Interface and driver behavior is hardware/version specific.
Professional and community guidance is context-bound and may disagree.
Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.

logic_guidance.listen_for: the performer-to-monitor response becoming more immediate without clicks, dropouts, or instability
logic_guidance.location: Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > Devices > I/O Buffer Size
logic_guidance.risk: overloading the CPU or causing clicks
logic_guidance.show_me_query: Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > Devices > I/O Buffer Size
logic_guidance.starting_point: Preserve the current state and test one stage or behavior at a time.
steps: Save a Project Alternative or duplicate the affected track, take folder, comp, or recording setup; document the current device, buffer, monitoring, routing, recording, and region state.
Save the current setting, bypass unnecessary live processing, lower the I/O buffer one step, and compare the same monitored phrase.
Record or audition the same short representative passage, compare against the untouched baseline, and change no unrelated variable.
Listen and inspect for: the performer-to-monitor response becoming more immediate without clicks, dropouts, or instability.
Stop or back off if: overloading the CPU or causing clicks.
Restore the saved Project Alternative, duplicated track/comp, recording preference, routing, or monitoring state used as the baseline.
logic_guidance.stop_condition: Stop once the performer-to-monitor response becoming more immediate without clicks, dropouts, or instability and no new problem is introduced. Undo or choose the alternative if overloading the CPU or causing clicks.
logic_guidance.undo: Restore the saved Project Alternative, duplicated track/comp, recording preference, routing, or monitoring state used as the baseline.
logic_guidance.version_scope: Logic Pro 12.3 target; verify exact recording, monitoring, take-folder, cycle, punch, preference, and menu labels against the installed version.

A technically neat result may still make performance or monitoring feel less natural.
A global preference or offset can solve one path while making another path worse.
user_intent: Use plug-in latency while recording correctly and preserve a reversible recording workflow.

canonical_question: Why does this happen: everything was fine until I added mastering plug-ins?
clarification_questions: Is the delayed thing a microphone/instrument monitor, a software instrument, or the placement of the recorded region?
Does the delay exist in an empty project, only through Logic, only through direct monitoring, or only after specific plug-ins are active?
What interface, sample rate, I/O buffer, monitoring path, Low Latency Mode state, and high-latency plug-ins are involved?

competing_hypotheses.description: plug-in latency while recording or another audio/MIDI stage is adding real monitoring or placement latency.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 1

competing_hypotheses.description: Duplicate monitoring, high-latency routing, driver/device state, or project complexity is being mistaken for one buffer problem.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 2

competing_hypotheses.description: temporarily disabling or using low-latency alternatives would provide a cleaner diagnostic or lower-latency recording path.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 3

direct_answer: A plug-in can add latency even when it is not obviously changing level; locate the first latency-heavy stage instead of blaming the performer. In Logic, first prove which stage or container owns the problem, then change only that stage and compare against the preserved baseline.
evidence_needed: The exact Logic version, device/interface, input/output routing, record and monitor state, relevant preferences, and current project/track/container state.
A preserved baseline plus one controlled test using the same performer, phrase, cue, and playback conditions.
Meters or recorded regions at each relevant signal-flow checkpoint, along with any audible delay, duplication, click, dropout, changed take, or placement error.
The user’s report of what improved, worsened, stayed unchanged, or became harder to perform after the test.
key_distinction: A plug-in can add latency even when it is not obviously changing level; locate the first latency-heavy stage instead of blaming the performer.
limitations: A meter, waveform, region position, or setting does not by itself prove the performer heard or recorded the intended result.
Interface and driver behavior is hardware/version specific.
Professional and community guidance is context-bound and may disagree.
Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.
This synthesized candidate is not yet promoted to reviewed knowledge.

logic_guidance.listen_for: the delay disappearing when the responsible latency path is removed
logic_guidance.location: mix bus, Stereo Out, and Low Latency Mode controls
logic_guidance.risk: bypassing the wrong processors or changing the mix permanently
logic_guidance.show_me_query: mix bus, Stereo Out, and Low Latency Mode controls
logic_guidance.starting_point: Preserve the current state and test one stage or behavior at a time.
steps: Save a Project Alternative or duplicate the affected track, take folder, comp, or recording setup; document the current device, buffer, monitoring, routing, recording, and region state.
Save a Project Alternative, bypass the mastering/mix-bus chain as a group, enable Low Latency Mode, and compare the same monitored phrase.
Record or audition the same short representative passage, compare against the untouched baseline, and change no unrelated variable.
Listen and inspect for: the delay disappearing when the responsible latency path is removed.
Stop or back off if: bypassing the wrong processors or changing the mix permanently.
Restore the saved Project Alternative, duplicated track/comp, recording preference, routing, or monitoring state used as the baseline.
logic_guidance.stop_condition: Stop once the delay disappearing when the responsible latency path is removed and no new problem is introduced. Undo or choose the alternative if bypassing the wrong processors or changing the mix permanently.
logic_guidance.undo: Restore the saved Project Alternative, duplicated track/comp, recording preference, routing, or monitoring state used as the baseline.
logic_guidance.version_scope: Logic Pro 12.3 target; verify exact recording, monitoring, take-folder, cycle, punch, preference, and menu labels against the installed version.
logic_guidance.visual_target_query: mix bus, Stereo Out, and Low Latency Mode controls

non_processing_possibilities: temporarily disabling or using low-latency alternatives

user_intent: Use correct input selection correctly and preserve a reversible recording workflow.

canonical_question: What transferable production principle should I learn from correct input selection?
clarification_questions: Does the interface hardware meter move, does the Logic track input meter move, and is a region actually recorded?

competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 3

direct_answer: Input selection must match the physical interface socket and channel numbering before track-level controls can help. In Logic, first prove which stage or container owns the problem, then change only that stage and compare against the preserved baseline.
evidence_needed: The exact Logic version, device/interface, input/output routing, record and monitor state, relevant preferences, and current project/track/container state.
A preserved baseline plus one controlled test using the same performer, phrase, cue, and playback conditions.
Meters or recorded regions at each relevant signal-flow checkpoint, along with any audible delay, duplication, click, dropout, changed take, or placement error.
The user’s report of what improved, worsened, stayed unchanged, or became harder to perform after the test.
key_distinction: Input selection must match the physical interface socket and channel numbering before track-level controls can help.
limitations: A meter, waveform, region position, or setting does not by itself prove the performer heard or recorded the intended result.
Interface and driver behavior is hardware/version specific.
Professional and community guidance is context-bound and may disagree.
Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.

logic_guidance.listen_for: only the intended input meter responding with the other channels silent
logic_guidance.location: channel-strip Input slot and interface input meter
logic_guidance.risk: recording the wrong channel or silence

logic_guidance.starting_point: Preserve the current state and test one stage or behavior at a time.
steps: Save a Project Alternative or duplicate the affected track, take folder, comp, or recording setup; document the current device, buffer, monitoring, routing, recording, and region state.
Speak into the microphone while selecting candidate mono inputs one at a time and confirm the expected meter responds.
Record or audition the same short representative passage, compare against the untouched baseline, and change no unrelated variable.
Listen and inspect for: only the intended input meter responding with the other channels silent.
Stop or back off if: recording the wrong channel or silence.
Restore the saved Project Alternative, duplicated track/comp, recording preference, routing, or monitoring state used as the baseline.
logic_guidance.stop_condition: Stop once only the intended input meter responding with the other channels silent and no new problem is introduced. Undo or choose the alternative if recording the wrong channel or silence.
logic_guidance.undo: Restore the saved Project Alternative, duplicated track/comp, recording preference, routing, or monitoring state used as the baseline.
logic_guidance.version_scope: Logic Pro 12.3 target; verify exact recording, monitoring, take-folder, cycle, punch, preference, and menu labels against the installed version.
logic_guidance.visual_target_query: channel-strip Input slot and interface input meter
